label: late original-phase n/c/f/s/w/q/l in sequences starting with p/i/g/j/o/m/t
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at t<2, at the delimiter, or during copy. Mostly fires at t>=3. Rate and mass rise toward the end of the input: about half the mass is on the last original token (to_go=0) and it is strongest in long sequences (L=8-9). It is driven by the current input token: n, c, f, and to a lesser extent s, w, q, l (these seven carry about 90% of the mass), and it prefers first occurrences. It is gated by sequence history: it is much more likely when the sequence starts with p, i, g, j, o, m or t (first_tok lift 2.4-3.8x), and orig(1) from the same set also helps. The history dependence looks graded rather than boolean, and the n_seen counts were worse than first_tok alone, so precision is limited. Top activations are runs of n/c/f/s near the end of long sequences that start with p/m/g/t/j/o/i, often building up over consecutive steps. It rarely fires on vowels, digits 0/2/3, or other letters.
